Great idea. Easy, low-maintenance plants can really warm up a place without adding a lot of work. Since your balcony gets good morning sun, you’ve got lots of good options. Here are some beginner-friendly picks and a quick care guide.

Top easy-care plant options (great for indoors or a sunny balcony)
- Snake plant (Sansevieria trifasciata)
  - Light: tolerates bright or low light; loves a sunny spot.
  - Water: very drought-tolerant; water every 2–3 weeks, less in winter. Allow soil to dry between waterings.
  - Why it’s good: nearly impossible to kill; architectural vertical leaves.

- Pothos (Epipremnum aureum)
  - Light: prefers bright indirect light but tolerates lower light.
  - Water: water when the top inch of soil is dry; can go a bit longer between waterings.
  - Why it’s good: trailing habit adds motion and interest; easy to train onto a shelf or small trellis.

- ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia)
  - Light: handles low to bright indirect light.
  - Water: thrives with infrequent watering; every 2–3 weeks is common.
  - Why it’s good: very tough, with glossy leaves and a compact look.

- Spider plant (Chlorophytum comosum)
  - Light: bright indirect light is ideal; tolerates a range.
  - Water: moderate; keep soil lightly moist but don’t waterlog. Let the top inch dry between waterings.
  - Why it’s good: forgiving, produces “pups” you can propagate to make new plants.

- Jade plant or small succulent (Crassula ovata or Haworthia)
  - Light: loves bright sun; place on a sunny balcony or windowsill.
  - Water: very infrequent; water when the soil is completely dry.
  - Why it’s good: nice compact shape; very low fuss when given sun and well-draining soil.

Quick care tips
- Containers and drainage: choose pots with drainage holes and a saucer underneath to catch excess water.
- Soil matter: use a standard potting mix with good drainage; avoid heavy loyalty soils for succulents.
- Light placement: group plants with similar light needs together; place the sun-loving ones where they’ll get that morning sun.
- Watering habit: it’s better to water more sparsely than too often. When in doubt, wait an extra day or two and check the soil.
- Dusting: wipe leaves occasionally with a damp cloth to keep them breathing well and looking tidy.
- Seasonal care: most indoors will do fine with half-strength fertilizer once a month during growing season (spring/summer) and none in winter.

A simple starter plan for your condo
- Pick 2–3 plants to start (e.g., a snake plant for a tall touch, a pothos for some trailing greens, and a spider plant for a forgiving, airy look).
- Get two good, lightweight containers with drainage for the balcony and one smaller indoor pot for a shelf or table.
- Place the snake plant and pothos near a sunny spot on the balcony or indoors by a window to start; tuck the spider plant where it can trail a bit or sit on a shelf.
- Set a simple routine: check soil moisture every 1–2 weeks; water only when the top inch is dry.
